sceneEn: A friend has invited you out for Saturday evening but you cannot go. Turn it down politely, give your reason and suggest another date instead.
partnerEn: a friend who is a little hurt at being turned down but understands
openingEn: You are coming on Saturday, aren't you?
goalEn: The refusal has been given politely, the reason has been put in a subordinate clause and a new date has been agreed.

sceneEn: You have run into a friend at a celebration. Pay them a compliment and let them pay you one; talk about how a compliment is answered too.
partnerEn: a modest friend who deflects a compliment straight away
openingEn: Oh, you look really good today! Is that new?
goalEn: Both of you have paid a compliment, at least one has been answered and the conversation has moved on to something else.

sceneEn: You had an argument with a friend yesterday and you have rung today to talk. Say what happened, apologise and suggest making up.
partnerEn: a friend who is still a little hurt but open to talking
openingEn: Hello. I'll be honest, I'm still a bit cross. What happened yesterday?
goalEn: The incident has been described, an apology has been made, it has been explained that it was not deliberate and the two of you have made up.

sceneEn: A friend is asking about your family being far away. Say how and how often you are in touch with them, and say what you miss most.
partnerEn: a curious friend whose own family lives nearby
openingEn: Your family lives so far away. How often are you in touch?
goalEn: How and how often you keep in touch has been described, what you miss most has been said and your friend has made a suggestion.

sceneEn: You are talking about your new year's resolutions with a friend on New Year's Eve. Give at least two goals and argue about whether one of them is realistic.
partnerEn: a sceptical friend who breaks their resolutions every year
openingEn: And? Have you set yourself anything for this year?
goalEn: Two goals have been given, the realism of one has been argued over and you have both agreed on one resolution.

sceneEn: A friend is asking what you do in your free time. Describe your habits with conditional clauses: what you do if the weather is fine, what you do if you have time.
partnerEn: a friend who has as little free time as you
openingEn: So what do you do when you get some time off?
goalEn: At least two habits have been described with conditional clauses and your friend has told you a habit of their own.

sceneEn: A friend is looking for something to watch. Recommend a series to them, describe the story briefly and say when you like watching.
partnerEn: a friend who watches something every evening but cannot choose
openingEn: I just can't find anything to watch. Have you got a recommendation?
goalEn: A series has been recommended, its story has been described and your friend has decided whether to watch it.

sceneEn: You have heard a news story and you are telling a friend. Say where you heard it, let them meet it with doubt, and discuss together whether it is true.
partnerEn: a friend who doubts every story they hear
openingEn: Tell me, have you heard that too? Is it really true?
goalEn: The story has been passed on, its source has been named, the doubt has been voiced and it has been decided how to check it.

sceneEn: You and a friend are talking about how much time you spend on your phones. Say which app you use and when, and say whether you want to cut it down.
partnerEn: a friend who never puts their phone down
openingEn: Look at this, my screen time — six hours. How much is yours?
goalEn: The way you use it has been described with conditional clauses and an opinion has been given about cutting it down.

sceneEn: You still have not had an answer to an application and you are ringing to ask. Say what you are waiting for, say how long you have been waiting and ask when you will hear.
partnerEn: a clerk on the phone who has to look it up on the system
openingEn: Good afternoon, what can I do for you?
goalEn: What you are waiting for and how long has been said, the clerk has given a date and that date has been confirmed.

sceneEn: A friend is having a problem with their computer and has rung you. Find out what the problem is and tell them step by step what to do.
partnerEn: a friend in a panic who does not know much about computers
openingEn: My computer's gone completely mad! Can you help me?
goalEn: The problem has been understood, instructions in at least three steps have been given and it has been found out whether the problem is solved.

sceneEn: You are back from holiday and showing a friend the photos on your phone. Describe each photo briefly and say which one you like best.
partnerEn: a friend who looks at the photos and asks questions
openingEn: Oh, show me! Where was that, then?
goalEn: At least three photos have been described, the favourite has been chosen and the reason has been given.

sceneEn: You are recommending a podcast you listen to. Describe what it is about, say why it is worth it and ask what they are interested in.
partnerEn: a friend looking for something to listen to on the way
openingEn: I need something for the journey to work. Do you listen to podcasts at all?
goalEn: A podcast has been recommended, its subject and its value have been described and your friend's interests have been found out.

sceneEn: You are in a formal video call and there is a problem with the sound. Report the problem, suggest a fix and settle how the meeting will carry on.
partnerEn: an official running the meeting
openingEn: Good afternoon, can you hear me all right?
goalEn: The technical problem has been reported, a fix has been tried and it has been settled how the meeting will carry on.

sceneEn: You did not turn your phone on all day and a friend is curious. Say what you did, how you felt at first and what you thought in the end.
partnerEn: a friend who wants to try the same but does not dare
openingEn: Nobody could reach you yesterday. What were you doing?
goalEn: What you did all day has been described, the feeling at the start and at the end has been given, and your friend has said whether they will try it.

sceneEn: You have moved to a new city and come to register your address. Say what you want, ask which documents are needed and find out when you will get the certificate.
partnerEn: a clerk behind the counter who asks step by step
openingEn: Good afternoon. What can I do for you?
goalEn: The registration has been requested, the documents needed have been found out and it has been settled when the certificate will be ready.

sceneEn: You are filling in a form at an office but you do not understand some of the fields. Ask the clerk, find out what to write and finish the form.
partnerEn: a clerk who explains the form line by line
openingEn: You can fill the form in here. Is there anything you're not sure about?
goalEn: At least two fields have been asked about and explained, and the form has been finished and handed in.

sceneEn: You had an appointment but you have waited two hours at the office. Explain the situation to the clerk, ask what happened and find out where to send a written complaint.
partnerEn: a clerk overwhelmed by the rush but still polite
openingEn: I'm sorry it's taken so long today. What was it you needed?
goalEn: The wait has been described, the reason has been found out and it is clear where a written complaint should go.

sceneEn: You want to join the library. Ask what is needed, find out how many books you can take and for how long, and look for a book.
partnerEn: an assistant who explains the library rules
openingEn: Good afternoon! Would you like to apply for a card?
goalEn: The joining conditions and the loan period have been found out, a book has been looked for and one rule has been confirmed.

sceneEn: You have come to the adult education centre and you want to enrol on a course. Ask which courses they offer, find out when it starts and enrol.
partnerEn: an adviser holding the course programme
openingEn: Good afternoon! Are you interested in a particular course?
goalEn: A course has been chosen, the start date and the timetable have been found out and the enrolment has been completed.

sceneEn: You and a friend are talking about your plans for the coming years. Describe at least two goals in the future tense and say why one of them matters.
partnerEn: a friend who describes their own plans too
openingEn: And where do you see yourself in five years?
goalEn: At least two goals have been described in the future tense, one has been justified and your friend has given their own plan.

sceneEn: You are talking to an adviser at the job centre. Say which occupation you want and why, and ask what steps are needed.
partnerEn: an adviser who guides people through choosing a career
openingEn: Tell me: what would you like to do for a living?
goalEn: An occupation and the reason for it have been given, the training needed has been found out and a next step has been agreed.

sceneEn: A German friend is asking whether you have settled in here. Describe two things you find strange and compare them with how it is in your own country.
partnerEn: a friend who wants to see their own country from the outside
openingEn: Tell me honestly: what struck you most here?
goalEn: At least two observations have been described in comparative form and your friend has given their own view.

sceneEn: You have an exam tomorrow and you are talking to a friend. Say how you have prepared, say how nervous you are and get some advice from your friend.
partnerEn: a friend who has taken the same exam and is trying to calm you down
openingEn: Tomorrow's the day. Are you nervous?
goalEn: The preparation has been described, the nerves have been voiced and your friend has given a concrete piece of advice.

sceneEn: It is the last day of the course and your teacher is asking what you have learnt this term. Say what you have managed, what is still hard and what you will do next.
partnerEn: a teacher closing the term who is proud of their student
openingEn: That was our last day of the course. What can you do now that you couldn't do before?
goalEn: At least two gains and one difficulty have been described and the next step has been given.
